brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases at cells (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1), all at level 0 (piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0, piece:0,1,0).

Two notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at the empty positions (-1,1) and (1,-1), each touching two of the bases. The family 'drawer' had no offers on any half-base configuration I tried, so I used the notch drawer frame instead, which the configurator accepted.
setNotchOpen applied to the notch at (1,-1), k=4, open=true. The notch at (-1,1) stays closed. I did not read back a distinct open state from get_build, so this rests on the apply result.
check_build: ok, no error issues, meshClash 'clear'. Only an info note about open cap faces remains.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet (three full hex bases in a triangle) with two notch drawer frames in the open positions on either side of the cluster. One drawer is set open. check_build is clear with no errors. Caveat: the requested drawer family did not offer any placement. I used the notch drawer frame, which is the configurator's drawer-type part for an empty position between two cells. The cabinet has no covers or caps, so it is open on the exposed faces.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
